summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of Addison’s disease was admitted for nausea, diarrhea, fatigue, and headache after overexertion, symptoms typical of an adrenal insufficiency flare. She had not eaten since the prior morning and presented with low sodium, managed with IV fluids and a 20 mg prednisone burst. Symptoms improved rapidly, with resolution of nausea, headache, and normalization of sodium. She tolerated oral intake and was discharged the following day with a steroid taper plan and instructions to follow up with endocrinology. No complications occurred during the admission.
problems: Other and unspecified noninfectious gastroenteritis and colitis
